neighbours.label: ' control' (or ' certain') closing a clause about what lies within one's power or is known for sure ('the things you can control')
fire: Stop worrying about the weather and work on what you can control.
Stoics teach us to accept the things we cannot control.
Put your energy into the parts of life you actually control.
There is so much I cannot change, so I focus on what I control.
The coach told the team to play hard and handle what they could control.
In a crisis, sort your worries into what you can and cannot control.
Amid all the rumours, the only thing that seemed certain was the deadline.
Let go of outcomes and look after the few things within your control.
quiet: The driver lost control of the truck on the icy bend.
She grabbed the remote control and turned on the news.
Air traffic control cleared the plane for landing.
Pest control came to the house on Tuesday morning.
A certain number of tickets are held back for members.
The control group received a sugar pill instead.
He reached for the volume control on the old radio.
Quality control found a fault in the new batch.

notes: Top examples: 'Focus on the things that you have control', 'well established', 'the only certain outcome'. Probe: 'what you can control' 0.72, 'One thing is certain' 0.18, noun 'lost control' ~0.
